title: Event logs, checkpoints and replay contracts

objectives.text: Define bounded versioned source/sequence event identity and exact duplicate/conflict handling without confusing command intent with external execution facts.

Use an explicit SQL transaction to commit event plus applied-cursor/projection together,demonstrate controlled rollback,and explain the additional file/settings/storage/recovery evidence required for durability.

blocks.markdown: A log must explain what happened under which schema,source/session/order namespace and ordering rule. Include event version,identity,units,payload meanings and required historical rule/reference inputs. A command is intent,not proof a venue accepted or filled it. Never reinterpret old payloads under new rules silently;define versioned readers/upcasters/migrations with retained originals and replay fixtures. Our count event(version,sequence,source,delta)is an own miniature schema,not FIX or a durable exchange journal.

Own schema1,sourceSIM1,sequence1..16,exact integer delta-10..10. Initial count10;projection(value,through_seq)uses inclusive last-applied cursor. An exact stored sequence/content retry returns duplicate;different content conflicts;new events must be next contiguous sequence and keep count0..100. One private database,one caller,one namespace,<=16events. SQL primary key enforces sequence uniqueness here;real multi-source IDs must include the actual namespace. Malformed fields are rejected before beginning. Bound SQL parameters transport values;do not build SQL by interpolating event text.

blocks.title: Insert and projection are one commit boundary

steps.text: Initial journal empty,through0,value10. Event1 delta+2 commits both event row and projection(1,12). These must not be published as independent successful writes.
Event2 delta+3 is inserted and projection changed to(2,15)inside an explicit transaction. Inject failure before COMMIT:ROLLBACK restores both to event1/(1,12). No acknowledged append2 exists.
Retry event2 without failure commits(2,15);exact retry is duplicate,no extra delta. The demo remains in memory and disappears on close. Catching an exception is not an OS crash or power-loss test.

blocks.caption: Expected:appended;rolled back;1 (1, 12);appended;duplicate;(2, 15). Python3.12+ sqlite3,local tested SQLite3.53.1. MEMORY database:SQL rollback/atomic event+projection demonstration,NOT file persistence,power-loss test or durable checkpoint. App runnable disabled until sqlite3/Python capability is verified. Single private connection/database;not an arbitrary schema validator or network broker adapter.

blocks.markdown: This example explicitly uses Python3.12 sqlite3.connect(autocommit=True),then SQL BEGIN IMMEDIATE/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. In this mode Python Connection.commit()/rollback()have no effect,so do not replace the SQL commands blindly. No executescript is used inside the transaction. BEGIN IMMEDIATE can fail busy if a different writer holds the database;production retry must preserve identity,reload/revalidate and have bounded backoff. The private in-memory connection tests no competing writers. The transaction prevents the demonstrated partial local state,not unrelated external sends.

A recovery checkpoint must pair state with exactly the applied prefix plus schema/source/session/reducer/configuration. The projection row here updates its cursor and count in the same event transaction. Rebuilding from ordered events can independently verify that projection matches its prefix. A database WAL checkpoint is a different storage operation transferring WAL content toward the main database;it is not automatically an application snapshot contract. Do not conflate WAL checkpoint completion with authenticated coherent strategy state.

To persist beyond process exit,use a file-backed database with an intentional supported journal/synchronous policy,transaction completion/error handling,backups and tested restore. SQLite documents atomic commit and the assumptions it needs from OS/filesystem/storage flush behavior;turning off journaling/synchronization changes safety. A Python flush,successful close or renamed JSON file alone is not proof of durable event+cursor commit across power loss. Do not copy only an active database main file while omitting required journal/WAL state;use a supported consistent backup procedure. This lesson does not execute or certify file/WAL/backup/power-loss recovery.

A local COMMIT cannot atomically guarantee that a remote venue executed an order exactly once. If committed intent must later cause an external effect,use a separately specified durable outbox/effect dispatcher with remote-supported identities,retry/unknown-outcome policy and reconciliation. Replaying old events must rebuild local state without resending old orders. Checksums can detect some corruption but do not authenticate source or prove schema meaning. Reject/hold unsupported versions,gaps or conflicts rather than quietly skipping them while advancing the applied cursor.

Independent transfer:enumerate bounded valid delta logs,compare ordered event sum with projection,and repeat every accepted ID exactly. Inject failure after insert and after projection for every next event;check journal+projection unchanged,then retry once and compare with clean reference. Separately design file-backed process-kill/reopen tests and storage fault tests without calling controlled exceptions power failure. State exact durability settings and source boundaries before claiming recovery readiness.

Sources:[Python3.12 sqlite3 transaction modes](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/sqlite3.html),[SQLite transactions](https://www.sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html),[atomic commit and storage assumptions](https://www.sqlite.org/atomiccommit.html),[isolation](https://www.sqlite.org/isolation.html),[PRAGMA settings](https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html),[event sourcing tradeoffs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/patterns/event-sourcing). Concrete schema/bounds are own model. SQL transaction semantics do not turn this memory demonstration into a durable live trading service.

summary: Versioned source-bound event semantics and consistent state/cursor matter. Commit event plus projection in one local transaction;test rollback,duplicates and replay. In-memory SQL,controlled exceptions and local commit do not prove file durability,power-loss recovery or remote exactly-once effects.
